title: Past simple
tagline: One tense for finished actions at a finished time: yesterday, last week, in 2019.
why: The past simple tells people what happened: your weekend, your holiday, a story for Writing Part 7. Cambridge loves finished-time words like yesterday and last year, and it expects was/were or the right -ed or irregular form. Get the spelling and the question word order right and your stories sound natural, not like a list of facts.

hook.text: Saturday. Mateo and Nadia are at the beach. "I swam for an hour!" says Mateo. "And I found a crab," says Nadia. "Did you see it, Sofia?" "No, I didn't — I was asleep!"
hook.ask: The past simple has three shapes here: an irregular verb, a helper verb (did) and was. Can you find them all?

diagrams.title: A finished action, a finished time
diagrams.caption: Past simple = a finished action at a finished time: yesterday, last week, in 2019, two days ago.

diagrams.title: Build the sentence in the past
diagrams.caption: In negatives and questions the helper did carries the past — the main verb goes back to its base form, even for irregular verbs.

diagrams.title: Adding -ed

rules.rule: Short verb, one vowel + one consonant: double it

diagrams.caption: Irregular verbs don't follow these rules — you just have to learn them: go → went, see → saw, have → had.

use.point: What you did yesterday or last week — regular verbs

examples.note: watch already ends in a consonant, just add -ed

use.point: was and were — the past of be

examples.note: did + base verb, no -ed in the question

watch_out.wrong: I go to the beach yesterday.
watch_out.why: Yesterday needs the past form of the verb, not the present.
The negative uses didn't + base verb — not is never alone before the verb.
Did already shows the past. The main verb goes back to its base form — no -ed after did.
Visit is followed directly by the person — no to.
Don't mix was with a base verb for a past action — just use the past simple verb.

l1.wrong: I go to the beach yesterday.
l1.why: Spanish can tell a recent story with the present, but English always needs the past form with yesterday.
The negative helper didn't goes before the verb; you can't just add not.
English questions need the helper did at the front, not just moving the verb.

l1.es: Hace dos años fuimos a Cusco.
l1.wrong: Ago two years, we went to Cusco.
l1.right: Two years ago we went to Cusco.
l1.why: Ago goes after the time word (two years ago); hace does not translate word for word.

l1.es: El año pasado fuimos a la playa.
l1.wrong: The past year we went to the beach.
l1.right: Last year we went to the beach.
l1.why: 'El año pasado' is last year in English, not 'the past year'.

remember.trick: -ed for regular, a new word for irregular!
remember.tip: If a verb doesn't end in -ed, it's probably irregular — go/went, see/saw, have/had. Learn them in small groups.

dialogue.title: What did you do at the weekend?
dialogue.context: Monday morning. Miss Vega asks the class about their weekend at the beach.

lines.speaker: Miss Vega
lines.text: Good morning! Did you have a good weekend?

lines.speaker: Mateo
lines.text: Yes! I went to the beach with my family.

lines.speaker: Mateo
lines.text: I swam for an hour and I played volleyball.

lines.speaker: Nadia
lines.text: I found a crab on the sand! It was huge.

lines.speaker: Nadia
lines.text: No, I wasn't. It didn't move very fast.

lines.speaker: Miss Vega
lines.text: Great stories! Sofia, what about you?

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.text: I didn't go anywhere. I stayed at home and I studied for the test.

can_do: I can talk about things that happened yesterday, last week or last year using the past simple.
I can make negatives and questions with didn't and Did…?.
I can use was and were and the most common irregular verbs (went, saw, had, found).
summary: Past simple = a finished action at a finished time: yesterday, last week, in 2019, two years ago.
Regular verbs add -ed (watch the spelling: stop → stopped, study → studied); irregular verbs change completely (go → went, see → saw).
Was/were is the past of be: I/he/she/it → was, you/we/they → were.
Negative: didn't + base verb. Question: Did + person + base verb — never add -ed after did.
Learn the irregular verbs in small groups — they don't follow a spelling rule.
